workerDeduplicationRule: Flattened page/worker Network events are coalesced only by the documented CDP requestId. No URL- or size-based merge and no synthetic response/data/terminal event is used.
workerWireSizeLimitation: The split page/worker CDP lifecycle reports the complete decoded Worker size (3970 B) and a real loadingFinished event, but encodedDataLength does not separate HTTP headers from the gzip body. The HAR preserves the observed _encodedDataLength, sets Worker response.headersSize/bodySize to -1, omits content.compression and marks _wireBodySizeKnown=false. Byte budgets are calculated independently from current dist.
note: Live CDP WebSocket capture; no event ring buffer was used. Successful HTTP resources are the editor document-graph size inventory. Served HTML is byte-bound to current dist and contains one exact Tiny core preload with no executable Tiny script; document-start instrumentation plus the fixed phe:bootstrap:* PerformanceMark sequence prove one runtime script and one preloaded resource become available before initialise after skeleton FP/FCP. The three local timing metrics end at the diagnostic phe:bootstrap:editor-ready mark and reconcile that mark to sampled nonzero DOM-ready state within 100 ms; they are not labelled as the deployed Slow-4G §7 input-readiness measurement. The cumulative scenario executes the complete E2 document-tool inventory plus E3 emoji, HTML/DOCX import, HTML export, clipboard, sample, draft and new-document actions. The isolated E5 browser proves the single About menu, real native new-page targets with null openers for both links, inline UTF-8 text/plain notices, light-only theme queries, exact About/Link-dialog blue and soft-blue states, native accent-color, responsive layouts, 44px coarse-pointer targets, computed contrast, focus, loading and DOCX busy states, and visualViewport updates without adding requests to either byte inventory. Both About destinations are independent top-level browsing contexts rather than resources consumed by the editor document graph, so their native-tab and HTTP-delivery proofs are deliberately separate from editor cold/cumulative payload accounting.
